paragraphs: Some of the statements in this document and any documents incorporated by reference, including any statements as to operational and financial projections, constitute "forward-looking statements" within the meaning of Section 21E of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the "Exchange Act") and Section 27A of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended. These statements relate to future events or our future financial performance and involve known and unknown risks, uncertainties and other factors that may cause our businesses' or our industries' actual results, levels of activity, performance or achievements to be materially different from those expressed or implied by any forward-looking statements. Such statements may address our plans, our strategies, our prospects, changes and trends in our business and the markets in which we operate under the heading "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" ("MD&A") or in other sections of this document. In some cases, you can identify forward-looking statements by terminology such as "may," "could," "would," "should," "expect," "plan," "anticipate," "intend," "believe," "estimate," "predict," "project," "potential" or "continue" or the negative of those terms or other comparable terminology. Particular risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ from those contained in the forward-looking statements, include the following: cyclical changes and specific industry events in our markets; changes in anticipated capital investment and maintenance expenditures by customers; changes in economic conditions in relevant global and North American markets, including as a result of the imposition, or threat of imposition of tariffs, including any new or increased tariffs announced by the U.S. government and any retaliatory tariffs announced in response thereto, and other trade barriers, international trade tensions or geopolitical conflicts; availability, limitations or cost increases of raw materials and/or commodities, including as a result of new or increased tariffs, as well as the potential impact of retaliatory tariffs and other penalties that cannot be recovered in product pricing; the impact of competition on profit margins and our ability to maintain or increase market share; risks with respect to our contracts with the U.S. government, including the government's ability to terminate contracts prior to completion or failure to appropriate amounts necessary to fund such contracts; inadequate performance by third-party suppliers and subcontractors for outsourced products, components and services and other supply-chain risks; the uncertainty of claims resolution with respect to environmental and other contingent liabilities; the impact of climate change and any legal or regulatory actions taken in response thereto; cyber-security risks; risks with respect to the protection of intellectual property, including with respect to our digitalization initiatives; the impact of overruns, inflation and the incurrence of delays with respect to long-term fixed-price contracts; defects or errors in current or planned products; the impact of pandemics and governmental and other actions taken in response; domestic economic, political, legal, accounting and business developments adversely affecting our business, including regulatory changes; uncertainties with respect to our ability to complete expansions to or the reconfiguration of our manufacturing footprint within the time periods and at costs we anticipate and whether we will realize the anticipated benefits of these activities; uncertainties with respect to our ability to identify acceptable acquisition targets; uncertainties surrounding timing and successful completion of acquisition transactions, including with respect to integrating acquisitions and achieving costs savings, synergistic sales or other benefits from acquisitions; the impact of retained liabilities of disposed businesses; potential labor disputes; and extreme weather conditions and natural and other disasters. These and other risks and uncertainties are further discussed in other sections of this document. These statements are only predictions. Actual events or results may differ materially because of market conditions in our industries or other factors, and forward-looking statements should not be relied upon as a prediction of actual results. In addition, management's estimates of future operating results are based on our current complement of businesses, which is subject to change as management selects strategic markets.

All the forward-looking statements are qualified in their entirety by reference to discussions of risks and uncertainties presented in this annual report, including under the heading "Risk Factors," and any subsequent filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission ("SEC"), as well as in any documents incorporated by reference that describe risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause results to differ materially from those projected in these forward-looking statements. We caution you that these discussions of risks and uncertainties may not be exhaustive. We operate in a continually changing business environment and frequently enter into new businesses and product lines. We cannot predict risk factors related to any future new business or product line, and we cannot assess the impact, if any, of such risk factors on our businesses or the extent to which any factor, or combination of factors, may cause actual results to differ materially from those projected in any forward-looking statements. You should not rely on forward-looking statements as a prediction of actual results. We disclaim any responsibility, except to the extent we are legally required, to update or publicly revise any forward-looking statements to reflect events or circumstances that arise after the date of this document.

SPX Technologies, Inc. ("SPX", "our", "the Company", or "we") is the successor registrant pursuant to Rule 12g-3(a) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, to SPX Corporation ("Legacy SPX") as a result of the completion on August 15, 2022 of a holding company reorganization (the "Holding Company Reorganization") effected as a merger of Legacy SPX with and into SPX Merger, LLC, a subsidiary of the Company. Each share of Legacy SPX's common stock, par value $0.01 per share, issued and outstanding immediately prior to the consummation of the Holding Company Reorganization was automatically converted into an equivalent corresponding share of the Company's common stock having the same designations, rights, powers and preferences and the qualifications, limitations and restrictions as the corresponding share of Legacy SPX common stock being converted. Accordingly, upon consummation of the Holding Company Reorganization, Legacy SPX stockholders became stockholders of the Company. Legacy SPX was founded in Muskegon, Michigan in 1912 as the Piston Ring Company and adopted the name SPX Corporation in 1988. Our common stock has been listed on the New York Stock Exchange since 1972. The terms "SPX," "we" and "our" include Legacy SPX for periods prior to the consummation of the Holding Company Reorganization as the context requires.

On September 26, 2015, we completed the spin-off to our stockholders (the "Spin-Off") of all the outstanding shares of SPX FLOW, Inc. ("SPX FLOW"), prior to the Spin-Off, a wholly-owned subsidiary of SPX, which at the time of the Spin-Off held the businesses comprising our Flow Technology reportable segment, our Hydraulic Technologies business, and certain of our corporate subsidiaries.

On November 1, 2022, SPX divested three wholly-owned subsidiaries that hold asbestos liabilities and certain assets, including related insurance assets, to Canvas Holdco LLC, an entity formed by a joint venture of Global Risk Capital LLC and an affiliate of Premia Holdings Ltd (the "Asbestos Portfolio Sale"). The divested subsidiaries have agreed to indemnify us and our affiliates for their asbestos-related liabilities, which encompassed all of our consolidated asbestos-related liabilities and contingent liabilities immediately prior to the divestiture. These indemnification obligations are not subject to any cap or time limitation. The board of managers of each of the divested subsidiaries received a solvency opinion from an independent advisory firm that the divested subsidiaries were solvent after giving effect to the Asbestos Portfolio Sale.

On April 3, 2023, we completed the acquisition of T.A. Morrison & Co. Inc. ("TAMCO"), a market leader in motorized and non-motorized dampers that control airflow in large-scale specialty applications in commercial, industrial, and institutional markets. The post-acquisition operating results of TAMCO are reflected within our HVAC reportable segment.

On June 2, 2023, we completed the acquisition of ASPEQ Heating Group ("ASPEQ"), a leading provider of electrical heating solutions to customers in industrial and commercial markets. The post-acquisition operating results of ASPEQ are reflected within our HVAC reportable segment.

On February 7, 2024, we completed the acquisition of Ingénia Technologies Inc. ("Ingénia"), which specializes in the design and manufacture of custom air handling units that demand high levels of precision and reliability in healthcare, pharmaceutical, education, food processing and industrial end markets. The post-acquisition operating results of Ingénia are reflected within our HVAC reportable segment.

On January 27, 2025, we completed the acquisition of Kranze Technology Solutions, Inc. ("KTS"), which specializes in digital interoperability and tactical networking solutions, primarily for the defense industry. The post-acquisition operating results of KTS are reflected within our Detection and Measurement reportable segment.

On April 15, 2025, we completed the acquisition of Sigma Heating and Cooling and Omega Heat Pump ("Sigma & Omega"), which specializes in highly engineered hydronic heating and cooling equipment, including vertical stack heat pumps and fan coils, institutional heating products, and both air-cooled and water-cooled commercial self-contained units. The post-acquisition operating results of Sigma & Omega are reflected within our HVAC reportable segment.

On January 20, 2026, we completed the acquisition of Thermolec Ltd. ("Thermolec"), which specializes in custom electric duct heating and related solutions. The post-acquisition results of Thermolec will be reflected within our HVAC reportable segment.

On February 6, 2026, we completed the acquisition of Crawford United Corporation ("Crawford"), which specializes in highly engineered air handling and industrial products. The post-acquisition results of Crawford's Commercial Air Handling Equipment businesses will be reflected within our HVAC reportable segment. Crawford's Industrial & Transportation Products businesses, which includes businesses serving aerospace, defense, transportation, and marine markets, is non-core to our long-term strategy. These non-core businesses will be recorded as assets held for sale, with their results reported as discontinued operations while we identify suitable buyer(s) and execute our plan to sell these businesses within twelve months.

Unless otherwise indicated, the description of our business provided in Part I pertains to continuing operations only (see Note 4 to our consolidated financial statements for information on discontinued operations). A description of the general development of our business, including with respect to developments occurring prior to those discussed above, is included in Item 1 of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024, which description is incorporated by reference.

We are a diversified, global supplier of highly specialized, engineered solutions serving the HVAC and detection and measurement markets. With operations in 16 countries and approximately 4,700 employees, we offer a wide array of highly engineered infrastructure products with strong brands.

headings: Risks Related to our Markets and Customers
Many of the markets in which we operate are cyclical or are subject to industry events, and our results have been and could be affected as a result.
Our business depends on capital investment and maintenance expenditures by our customers.
Our customers have been and could be impacted by commodity availability and prices.
We operate in highly competitive markets. Our failure to compete effectively could harm our business.
Our business with various governments is subject to government contracting risks.
Contracts with, or funded by, the U.S. government or their agencies present additional risks compared to contracts with private sector customers.
Risks Related to our Suppliers and Vendors
The price and availability of raw materials and components may adversely affect our business.

The fact that we outsource various elements of the products and services we sell subjects us to the business risks of our suppliers and subcontractors, which could have a material adverse impact on our operations.
Risks Related to Our Manufacturing and Operations
Cost overruns, inflation, delays and other risks could significantly impact our results, particularly with respect to fixed-price contracts.
Our operations are at risk of damage, destruction or disruption by natural disasters and other unexpected events.
Risks Related to Manufacturing Footprint Changes and Capacity Expansion.
Risks Related to Acquisitions and Dispositions
Acquisitions involve a number of risks and present financial, managerial and operational challenges.
Our failure to successfully complete acquisitions could negatively affect us.
We may not achieve the expected cost savings and other benefits of our acquisitions.
Dispositions or liabilities retained in connection with dispositions could negatively affect us.
We may be unable to effect dispositions of non-core businesses on attractive terms or at all.
Risks Related to Macro-Economic, Domestic and World Events
Governmental laws and regulations could negatively affect our business.
Difficulties presented by domestic economic, political, legal, accounting and business factors could negatively affect our business.
Worldwide economic conditions could negatively impact our businesses.
Our non-U.S. revenues and operations expose us to numerous risks that may negatively impact our business.
Climate change and legal or regulatory responses thereto may have an adverse impact on our business and results of operations.
Failure to meet evolving expectations for other reporting on sustainability and social responsibility matters could adversely affect our sales and results of operations.
Risks Related to Information, Technology and Cybersecurity
If we are unable to protect our information systems and networks against data corruption, cyber-based attacks or network security breaches, our operations could be disrupted.
Operation on multiple Enterprise Resource Planning ("ERP") information systems and other applications may negatively impact our operations and internal control environment.
Failure to protect or unauthorized use of our intellectual property may harm our business.
Risks Related to Contingent Liabilities
Our current and planned products may contain defects or errors that are detected only after delivery to customers. If that occurs, our reputation may be harmed and we may face additional costs.
We are subject to potential liability relating to claims, complaints and proceedings, including those relating environmental, product liability and other matters.
Risks Related to Human Capital Resources
The loss of key personnel and an inability to attract and retain qualified employees could have a material adverse effect on our operations.

We are subject to work stoppages, union negotiations, labor disputes and other matters associated with our labor force, which may adversely impact our operations and cause us to incur incremental costs.
Risks Related to Financial Matters
A significant portion of our debt accrues interest at variable rates and increases in applicable benchmark interest rates could adversely affect our results of operations and cash flows.
Currency conversion risk could have a material impact on our reported results of business operations.
Credit and counterparty risks could harm our business.
Currency and interest rate hedging activities may adversely impact our financial performance as a result of changes in relevant interest rates and currency rates.
Changes in tax laws and regulations or other factors could cause our income tax obligations to increase, potentially reducing our net income and adversely affecting our cash flows.
paragraphs: You should consider the risks described below and elsewhere in our documents filed with the SEC before investing in any of our securities. We may amend, supplement or add to the risk factors described below from time to time in future reports filed with the SEC.
Many of the markets in which we operate are subject to general economic cycles or industry events. In addition, certain of our businesses are subject to market-specific cycles.

Furthermore, contract timing on projects, including those relating to communication technologies, transportation systems, aids to navigation products, and process cooling systems and towers may cause significant fluctuations in revenues and profits from period to period.

The businesses of many of our customers are to varying degrees cyclical and have experienced, and may continue to experience, periodic downturns. Cyclical changes and specific industry events, including changes in demand for the construction of data centers, could also affect sales of products in our businesses. Downturns in the business cycles of our different operations may occur at the same time, which could exacerbate any adverse effects on our business. In addition, certain of our businesses have seasonal and weather-related fluctuations, particularly within certain of our heating products businesses within our HVAC reportable segment. Historically, many of our key businesses generally have tended to have stronger performance in the second half of the year. See "MD&A - Results of Continuing Operations and Results of Reportable Segments and Corporate Expense."

Demand for most of our products and services depends on the level of new capital investment and planned maintenance expenditures by our customers. The level of capital expenditures by our customers fluctuates based on planned expansions, new builds and repairs, commodity prices, general economic conditions, availability of credit, funding available from government sources, and expectations of future market behavior. Although to our knowledge no one customer accounted for more than 10% of our consolidated revenues, many of our businesses derive revenues from large projects or key customer relationships and any of the aforementioned factors, whether individually or in the aggregate, could have a material adverse effect on our customers and, in turn, our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

A number of factors outside our control, including fluctuating commodity prices, impact the demand for our products. Increased commodity prices, including as a result of new or increased tariffs or the impact of new trade laws, may increase our customers' cost of doing business, thus causing them to delay or cancel large capital projects.

paragraphs: Revenues for 2025 totaled $2,265.1, compared to $1,983.9 in 2024 (and $1,741.2 in 2023). The increase in revenues during 2025, compared to 2024, was due primarily to (i) inorganic revenue growth resulting from the Ingénia and Sigma & Omega acquisitions within the HVAC reportable segment and the KTS acquisition within the Detection and Measurement reportable segment and (ii) organic revenue growth within the HVAC and Detection and Measurement reportable segments. The increase in revenues during 2024, compared to 2023 was due primarily to (i) inorganic revenue growth resulting from the Ingénia, ASPEQ, and TAMCO acquisitions (each within the HVAC reportable segment) and (ii) organic revenue growth within the HVAC reportable segment.
For 2025, operating income totaled $350.4, compared to $308.3 in 2024 (and $221.9 in 2023).
Additional details on certain matters noted above as well as significant items impacting the financial results for 2025, 2024, and 2023 are as follows:
2025: •On January 27, 2025, we completed the acquisition of KTS

◦The purchase price for KTS was $340.0, inclusive of amounts related to future service obligations of certain existing employees of $46.5 and net of an adjustment to the purchase price of $2.4 received during 2025 related to acquired working capital.
◦The post-acquisition operating results of KTS are included within our Detection and Measurement reportable segment.
•On April 15, 2025, we completed the acquisition of Sigma & Omega
◦The purchase price for Sigma & Omega was $143.3, net of (i) an adjustment to the purchase price of $0.3 received during 2025 related to acquired working capital and (ii) cash acquired of $0.2.
◦The post-acquisition operating results of Sigma & Omega are included within our HVAC reportable segment.

◦On August 12, 2025, the Company entered into an underwriting agreement, pursuant to which the Company agreed to issue and sell in a registered public offering 3.059 shares of the Company's common stock, at a purchase price of $188.0 per share (the "Offering").
◦The net proceeds to the Company from the Offering, after deducting underwriting discounts, commissions, and offering expenses payable by the Company of $23.9, were $551.1.
◦On September 9, 2025, we amended and restated our senior credit agreement (as amended, the "Amended Credit Agreement").

paragraphs: 本文件及任何被引用文件中的一些陳述，包括任何有關營運及財務預測的陳述，屬於根據1934年證券交易法第21E條（「證券交易法」）及1933年證券法第27A條（「證券法」）所定義的「向前看陳述」。這些陳述涉及未來事件或我們未來財務表現，並包含已知及未知的風險、不確定性及其他因素，這些因素可能導致我們業務或產業的實際結果、活動水準、表現或成就與向前看陳述中所表達或暗示的有重大差異。這些陳述可能涉及我們的計畫、策略、前景、業務及我們經營之市場的變化與趨勢，並在「管理層對財務狀況及營運結果之討論與分析」（「MD&A」）或本文件其他部分中提及。在某些情況下，您可透過如「可能」、「可能」、「可能」、「應該」、「預期」、「計畫」、「預期」、「意圖」、「相信」、「估計」、「預測」、「預測」、「潛在」或「持續」或這些詞語的否定形式或其他相當詞語來辨識向前看陳述。可能導致實際結果與向前看陳述中所包含結果有重大差異的特定風險與不確定性，包括以下內容：我們市場中的週期性變化及特定產業事件；客戶預期的資本投資與維護支出的變化；相關全球及北美市場經濟條件的變化，包括因徵收或威脅徵收關稅，包括美國政府宣佈的新或增加關稅及任何因應之報復性關稅，以及其他貿易障礙、國際貿易緊張或地緣政治衝突；原材料及/或商品的可得性、限制或成本增加，包括因新或增加關稅所致，以及因報復性關稅及其他處罰無法透過產品價格回收的潛在影響；競爭對利潤率的影響及我們維持或增加市場佔有率的能力；與美國政府契約相關的風險，包括政府提前終止契約或未能適當撥款以資助這些契約的能力；第三方供應商及 subcontractors 對委外產品、零組件及服務的表現不足，以及其他供應鏈風險；環境及其他潛在責任的聲請解決的不確定性；氣候變遷的影響及任何因應之法律或監管行動；網路安全風險；與智慧財產權保護相關的風險，包括與我們數位化計畫相關的風險；長期固定價格契約中過度支出、通貨膨脹及延誤產生的影響；現有或計畫產品的缺陷或錯誤；疫情及政府及其他因應行動的影響；影響我們業務的國內經濟、政治、法律、會計及商業發展，包括監管變更；我們在預期時間內及預期成本內完成製造基地擴張或重新配置的不確定性，以及我們是否能實現這些活動的預期效益；我們識別可接受收購目標的不確定性；與收購交易的時間及成功完成相關的不確定性，包括整合收購及實現成本節省、協同銷售或其他收購效益的不確定性；保留的已出售業務負債的影響；潛在勞工爭議；以及極端天氣條件及自然及其他災難。

所有向前看陳述均應參考本年度報告中對風險與不確定性的討論，包括在「風險因素」標題下，以及任何隨後向美國證券交易委員會（「SEC」）提交的文件，以及任何被引用文件中描述可能導致結果與向前看陳述中預測結果有重大差異的風險、不確定性及其他因素。我們提醒您，這些風險與不確定性的討論可能並非詳盡無遺。我們處於不斷變化的商業環境中，並經常進入新的業務與產品線。我們無法預測與任何未來新業務或產品線相關的風險因素，也無法評估這些風險因素對我們業務的影響，或任何因素或因素組合可能導致實際結果與向前看陳述中預測結果有重大差異的程度。您不應依賴向前看陳述作為實際結果的預測。我們聲明對更新或公開修訂任何向前看陳述的責任，除非法律要求我們如此做。

SPX Technologies, Inc.（「SPX」、「我們」、「本公司」或「我們」）根據1934年證券交易法第12g-3(a)條，成為SPX Corporation（「Legacy SPX」）的繼承註冊人，這是因2022年8月15日完成的控股公司重組（「控股公司重組」）所致，該重組為Legacy SPX與SPX Merger, LLC（本公司子公司）的合併。在控股公司重組完成前，Legacy SP, Inc. 每一股普通股（面值每股0.01美元）自動轉換為本公司相同設計、權利、權力及優先權，以及相同資格、限制及限制的普通股。因此，在控股公司重組完成後，Legacy SPX股東成為本公司股東。Legacy SPX 於1912年在密歇根州Muskegon成立，最初為Piston Ring Company，並於1988年更名為SPX Corporation。我們的普通股自1972年起在紐約證券交易所上市。本文中「SPX」、「我們」及「我們」在需要的情況下，包括Legacy SPX在控股公司重組完成前的時期。
2015年9月26日，我們完成了將SPX FLOW, Inc.（「SPX FLOW」）所有發行在外股份分拆給股東（「分拆」）的行動，分拆前，SPX FLOW為SPX的 wholly-owned subsidiary，當時持有我們Flow Technology應報告分部、Hydraulic Technologies業務及部分公司子公司。

於 2022 年 11 月 1 日，SPX 將三個 wholly-owned 子公司出售給 Canvas Holdco LLC，該公司由 Global Risk Capital LLC 與 Premia Holdings Ltd 之附屬公司所共同設立之合資企業（"Asbestos Portfolio Sale"）。被出售之子公司已同意對我們及其附屬公司就其 asbestos 相關負債進行賠償，此負債涵蓋我們在出售前之所有合併 asbestos 相關負債及或有負債。此賠償義務不受任何上限或時間限制。被出售之每個子公司之董事會已從獨立顧問機構取得財務健全意見，認為在考量 Asbestos Portfolio Sale 後，被出售之子公司為財務健全。
於 2023 年 4 月 3 日，我們完成對 T.A. Morrison & Co. Inc.（"TAMCO"）之收購，TAMCO 為市場上在商業、工業及機構市場中控制大型專用應用之空氣流動之電動及非電動閥門之領導廠商。TAMCO 收購後之營運成果已納入我們之 HVAC 應報告分部。
於 2023 年 6 月 2 日，我們完成對 ASPEQ Heating Group（"ASPEQ"）之收購，ASPEQ 為工業及商業市場中電氣加熱解決方案之主要供應商。ASPEQ 收購後之營運成果已納入我們之 HVAC 應報告分部。
於 2024 年 2 月 7 日，我們完成對 Ingénia Technologies Inc.（"Ingénia"）之收購，Ingénia 專門從事醫療、藥品、教育、食品加工及工業等終端市場中高精度及高可靠度之自訂空氣處理單元之設計與製造。Ingénia 收購後之營運成果已納入我們之 HVAC 應報告分部。
於2025年1月27日，本公司完成對Kranze Technology Solutions, Inc.（"KTS"）的收購，KTS專門從事數位互通性及戰術網路解決方案，主要服務防禦產業。KTS收購後的營運成果已納入本公司Detection and Measurement應報告分部。
於2025年4月15日，本公司完成對Sigma Heating and Cooling and Omega Heat Pump（"Sigma & Omega"）的收購，Sigma & Omega專門從事高工程化水力加熱與冷卻設備，包括垂直堆疊熱泵與風盤、機構加熱產品，以及空氣冷卻與水冷卻商業自備單位。Sigma & Omega收購後的營運成果已納入本公司HVAC應報告分部。
於2026年1月20日，本公司完成對Thermolec Ltd.（"Thermolec"）的收購，Thermolec專門從事客製電動風管加熱及相關解決方案。Thermolec收購後的營運成果將納入本公司HVAC應報告分部。

於2026年2月6日，本公司完成對Crawford United Corporation（"Crawford"）的收購，Crawford專門從事高工程化空氣處理與工業產品。Crawford Commercial Air Handling Equipment業務收購後的營運成果將納入本公司HVAC應報告分部。Crawford Industrial & Transportation Products業務，包括服務航空、防禦、運輸與海事市場的業務，與本公司長期策略無關。這些非核心業務將被記為待售資產，其營運成果將作為已終止營運業務報告，同時本公司將尋找合適買家並執行出售這些業務的計畫，時間為十二個月內。
除非另有說明，Part I中所述本公司業務描述僅涉及持續營運（請參閱我們合併財務報表附註4以取得有關已終止營運業務的資訊）。本公司業務的總體發展情況，包括在上述討論之前發生的發展，請參閱我們2024年12月31日財年所提交的Form 10-K年度報告第1項，該描述已納入參考。
本公司為一家多元化、全球性供應商，提供高度專業化、工程化的解決方案，服務於HVAC及檢測與測量市場。本公司在16個國家設有營運據點，約有4,700名員工，提供廣泛的高工程化基礎設施產品，並擁有強勢品牌。

paragraphs: 營業收入於2025年總計為$2,265.1，較2024年的$1,983.9（以及2023年的$1,741.2）增加。2025年營業收入較2024年增加，主要係因(i)非營運性收入成長，來自於HVAC應報告分部內的Ingénia及Sigma & Omega收購，以及Detection and Measurement應報告分部內的KTS收購，以及(ii)營運性收入成長，來自於HVAC以及Detection and Measurement應報告分部。2024年營業收入較2023年增加，主要係因(i)非營運性收入成長，來自於HVAC應報告分部內的Ingénia、ASPEQ以及TAMCO收購，以及(ii)營運性收入成長，來自於HVAC應報告分部。

headings: 與我們市場及客戶相關的風險
我們所從事的許多市場具有週期性或受產業事件影響，因此我們的營運成果已受到影響，未來也可能因此受到影響。
我們的業務依賴客戶的資本投資及維護支出。
客戶已受到並可能繼續受到原物料供應及價格的影響。
我們所處的市場為高度競爭性市場。若我們無法有效競爭，將對我們的業務造成損害。
我們與各政府機構的業務面臨政府採購相關風險。
與美國政府或其機構簽訂的契約或由其資助的契約，相比與民間部門客戶的契約，具有額外的風險。
與我們供應商及經銷商相關的風險
原物料及零組件的價格與可得性可能對本公司業務產生不利影響。
本公司委外處理所銷售產品及服務的各項要素，使本公司承受供應商及 subcontractors 的商業風險，可能對本公司營運產生重大不利影響。
與本公司製造及營運相關的風險
成本超支、通貨膨脹、延誤及其他風險可能對本公司結果產生重大影響，特別是在固定價格合約方面。
本公司營運可能因天然災害及其他未預期事件而遭受損壞、破壞或中斷。
與製造據點變更及產能擴張相關的風險
與收購及處分相關的風險
收購涉及多項風險，並帶來財務、管理及營運上的挑戰
本公司未能成功完成併購，可能對我們產生負面影響。
本公司可能無法實現併購預期的成本節省及其他好處。
資產處置或因資產處置而保留的負債，可能對本公司產生負面影響。
本公司可能無法以具吸引力的條件或完全無法處置非核心業務。
與總體經濟、國內及國際事件相關的風險
政府法令與規範可能對本公司業務產生負面影響。
國內經濟、政治、法律、會計及商業因素所帶來的困難，可能對本公司業務產生負面影響。
全球經濟情勢可能對本公司業務產生負面影響。
本公司於非美國市場之營收與營運面所面臨之風險，可能對本公司業務造成負面影響。
氣候變遷及相關法律或法規之反應，可能對本公司業務及營運成果造成負面影響。
未能符合對永續性及社會責任事項之持續披露期待，可能對本公司銷售及營運成果造成負面影響。
與資訊、科技及網路安全相關之風險
若本公司無法保護資訊系統及網路免受資料毀損、基於網路之攻擊或網路安全漏洞之侵害，可能導致本公司營運受阻。
於多個企業資源規劃（"ERP"）資訊系統及其他應用程式上進行營運，可能對本公司營運及內部控制環境造成負面影響。
未能保護或遭未經授權使用本公司智慧財產權，可能對本公司業務造成損害。
與或有負債相關之風險
本公司目前及計畫中的產品可能含有缺陷或錯誤，僅在交付給客戶後才會被發現。若發生此情況，可能損害本公司聲譽，並導致本公司面臨額外成本。
本公司可能因聲請、投訴及訴訟等事項而面臨潛在責任，包括與環境、產品責任及其他事項相關的聲請、投訴及訴訟。
與人力資源相關的風險
關鍵人員的流失以及無法吸引並留住合資格員工，可能對本公司營運產生重大不利影響。
本公司可能因勞工罷工、工會談判、勞資爭議及其他與勞工相關事項而面臨風險，這些風險可能對本公司營運產生不利影響，並導致本公司產生額外成本。
與財務事項相關的風險
本公司大部分債務的利率為浮動利率，適用的基準利率上升可能對本公司營運成果及現金流產生不利影響。
貨幣兌換風險可能對本公司所報告的營運成果產生重大影響。
信用及交易對方風險可能影響本公司營運。
貨幣及利率避險活動可能因相關利率及貨幣匯率變動而對本公司財務表現造成負面影響。
稅法及規範變更或其他因素可能導致本公司所得稅義務增加，進而潛在降低本公司淨收入並對現金流造成負面影響。
paragraphs: 您在投資本公司任何證券前，應考慮下列所描述的風險，以及我們向 SEC 提交文件中其他部分所描述的風險。我們可能在未來向 SEC 提交的報告中，隨時修改、補充或增加 herein 所描述的風險因素。
我們營運的許多市場均受總體經濟週期或產業事件影響。此外，我們某些業務亦受特定市場週期影響。
此外，專案的合約時程，包括與通訊科技、運輸系統、導航輔助產品、製程冷卻系統及冷卻塔相關的專案，可能導致營業收入與利潤在不同期間出現顯著波動。

我們許多客戶的業務在不同程度上具有週期性，並已歷經，或可能持續歷經，週期性衰退。產業週期變化及特定產業事件，包括資料中心建設需求的變化，也可能影響我們業務中產品的銷售。我們不同業務的週期性衰退可能同時發生，這可能會加劇對我們業務的任何不利影響。此外，我們某些業務會因季節性及天氣因素而產生波動，特別是在我們 HVAC 應報告分部中某些加熱產品業務。歷史上，我們許多關鍵業務通常在年度第二季表現較佳。請參閱 "MD&A - 維持營運之結果及應報告分部與公司費用之結果"。

我們大多數產品與服務的需求取決於客戶的新增資本投資及預計維護支出水平。客戶的資本支出水平會根據預計擴張、新興建設及修繕、商品價格、總體經濟狀況、信貸可得性、來自政府的資金以及對未來市場行為的預期而變動。儘管我們所知，沒有任何客戶佔我們合併營收的 10% 以上，我們許多業務來自大型專案或關鍵客戶關係，而上述任何因素，無論個別或總體，都可能對客戶產生重大不利影響，進而影響我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果及現金流。
許多因素超出我們的控制範圍，包括商品價格波動，會影響我們產品的需求。商品價格上漲，包括因新或增加關稅或新貿易法規的影響，可能提高客戶的營運成本，導致客戶延後或取消大型資本專案。
